evidence.statement: The 16-bp exact core GTAGCGAAATTCCTTG occurs five times in E. coli, once in Pyrococcus, and once in the S. cerevisiae mitochondrial chromosome in the frozen raw recurrence output.
In E. coli and Pyrococcus the 16-bp core is nested at offset 4 inside LC-PRIM-0002.
Post-freeze annotation places the yeast mitochondrial occurrence at chrM position 59,837 (0-based) within the mitochondrial 21S large-subunit rRNA locus.
This is a validated cross-domain/deep-lineage large-subunit-rRNA-associated primitive and an observed example of a shorter primitive persisting where the longer parent block does not.
Published-sequence anchoring plus the frozen 119-bp spacing maps LC-PRIM-0003 to E. coli 23S rRNA positions 1930-1945.
This interval lies in the conserved Domain IV subunit-interface region near the peptidyl-transferase center and includes U1940; experimental U1940A mutation disrupts 50S/30S subunit association.
Coder alias: LSU_SUBUNIT_INTERFACE — a conserved token in machinery used to maintain large/small ribosomal subunit association.

unknowns: Whether this exact 16-bp core has one conserved mechanistic role across all three observed implementations.
